title: MCP Authorization: CIMD, Issuer Binding, PKCE, and Step-Up

questions.question: Which mechanism is preferred for new MCP OAuth client enrollment in 2026-07-28?
options: An access token in the URL
questions.explanation: CIMD is preferred; DCR is deprecated and retained as a compatibility path.

questions.question: What application_type should a desktop client with a loopback redirect declare during DCR fallback?
questions.explanation: Desktop, mobile, command-line, and loopback clients are native applications.

questions.question: What must a client do with an authorization response iss value?
options: Compare it exactly with the recorded issuer before using the response
questions.explanation: RFC 9207 issuer checking prevents authorization response mix-up between issuers.

questions.question: How should a client key issuer-minted OAuth credentials and access tokens?
options: Issuer-minted credentials by issuer and tokens by issuer plus resource
All registrations and tokens under one global client name
By the server display name only
questions.explanation: Issuer and resource keys prevent minted credentials from crossing security authorities or audiences. A self-hosted CIMD URL remains portable.

questions.question: A resource returns 403 with scope notes:delete. What is the correct next step?
options: Explain the scope, obtain consent, authorize for it, then retry with a new request id
Send the MCP token to a downstream API
Reuse the current token and ignore the challenge
questions.explanation: Step-up obtains a newly authorized token before retrying the operation.

questions.question: What is the RFC 9728 metadata URL for the MCP resource https://notes.example.com/mcp?
questions.explanation: RFC 9728 preserves the protected resource path after the well-known segment, so the /mcp suffix is required.
